title: Lane lint counts a PR clash only when both heads merge clean with main, and checks the head against main
why: merge --lane-lint's cross check fails a lane head that merged current main whenever an older sibling PR of the same lane session is stale against main; the conflict comes from main, not from the lane. Incidents 2026-11-10: #2563 (17:31 CST) blamed on #2573, and #2573 (18:24 CST) blamed on #2562 in hooks/guard_merge.py, a file #2573 does not touch; #2562 lacked main. #2566 passed lint at 17:06 CST while it conflicted with main itself.
note: Coordinator 14:05 CST Nov 10 queued it; coordinator 22:01 CST Nov 10: build it as a triage build with full review rounds. Fix (plan, opus, refuter opus 23:31 CST: revise, gaps folded in): lane lint checks the head against main (a conflict FAILs and names main); a pair clash counts only when both heads merge clean with main, else it is a report line naming the PR that conflicts with main; all steps run and give one verdict; an integration head's pair clashes are report lines. Departs from the first fix text (a file filter, or skip parked PRs): a stale sibling on the same file still clashes through main's hunk. Measured 23:33 CST: #2577's head clashed with #1426 and #2564, and each of those conflicts with main on the same files, so the main-net rule clears it. Red cases R1-R7 in merge/test_lane_lint.py CrossMeasure. Builder must say what the PR number is for a ref target in merge_reason. Folds in step lint-clash-blames-wrong-pr. #1487 waits on it.
